en.headline: Police activate AI facial recognition on SmartView CCTV network
en.dek: Commissioner Joe Chow said the system, starting Monday, would help identify suspects and deter crime, with authorisation required for use.
body: Hong Kong police activated artificial intelligence-powered facial recognition capabilities across their SmartView closed-circuit television network on Monday, as announced by Commissioner of Police Joe Chow Yat-ming.

Chow said the technology is intended to provide stronger protection for law-abiding residents and serve as a deterrent against criminal activity. It can assist in identifying people even if they wear masks or use other methods to evade detection, according to police.

Police said searches require approval from an officer of inspector rank or above and must be linked to crime prevention, public safety or national security. Ordinary CCTV footage is retained for up to 31 days, while data from facial recognition is kept for up to 180 days.
The network currently includes thousands of cameras, with plans to expand to around 60,000 by 2028. Four shopping malls have agreed to connect their systems, police said.

zh.headline: 警方啟用智慧监控系統AI人臉識別功能
zh.dek: 警務處處長周一正式啟用，指可協助識別嫌疑人及阻嚇罪案，使用須經授權。
body: 香港警方周一啟用人工智能人臉識別功能，應用於其「銳眼」閉路電視監控系統，警務處處長周一正早前宣佈。
周一正表示，技術旨在為守法市民提供更強保護，並作為對犯罪活動的阻嚇。警方指，即使嫌疑人戴口罩或使用其他方法避避，系統仍可協助識別。
警方表示，使用人臉識別須經督察級以上人員批准，並只限於預防罪案、公共安全或國家安全。一般閉路電視影像保存最長不超過31天，人臉識別數據則最長180天。
系統現時包括數千部攝像機，計劃於2028年擴展至約6萬部。警方指，已有四家商場同意接入其攝像機系統。
